subject: SAMPLE: three businesses, one trick: own the thing that gets reordered
title: Week in patterns (sample)
intro: SAMPLE DATA. This week's placeholder businesses all made money on the second purchase, not the first.

principles.principle: The first sale buys permission for the tenth.
principles.evidence: Sample evidence tying this to the week's businesses.

archetype_map: Razor-and-blades and subscription/consumable are cousins; both sell a moment of excitement and then a stream of boredom.
through_line: Design the boring part so only you can sell it.
action: Look at your last three purchases and ask which one the seller actually made money on.
audio_script: This is The Daily Teardown, Sunday edition, and this is a sample, so nothing here is real. This week the pattern was simple: the money was in the second purchase, not the first. ... Take a second and think about the last three things you bought. Which one did the seller actually make money on? ... Razor and blades and consumable subscriptions are cousins. Both sell a moment of excitement and then a stream of boredom, and the boredom is where the margin lives. The through-line for the week: design the boring part so only you can sell it. That's the sample Sunday edition. Back tomorrow.
